title: KB's Raw Prawns, Tail On, Large, 500g $12.00 (Was $24.00, 50% off) @ Coles
body:
Deal: KB's Raw Prawns, Tail On, Large, 500g $12.00 (Was $24.00, 50% off) @ Coles

[CabSav] Produced in Vietnam
Yeah, nahhhh, we have lovely prawns here in Oz thanks.
[Lizard Spock] Agreed. Incidentally, I tried to speak Vietnamese once, but my prawn-unciation was terrible.
[QuickToThePointless] You should invest more time - I think it’s shellfish of you to expect Vietnamese to learn your language.
[TurkeyBargain] +1
If I'm going to buy frozen prawns from Coles, I'd much rather buy Karumba (wild-caught in the Gulf of Carpentaria) for $18-22/kg.
[CabSav] $24/kg ..?
For Produced in Vietnam ?
Not a bargain
[Lizard Spock] Prediction: jv will comment something like "Don't come the raw prawn with me".
[Bignudge] I've always wondered… what makes these prawns have a springy crunch when bitten into?
[QuickToThePointless] They are sustainably sourced from the finest 100% pure Vietnamese open sewer water the region has to offer
[revheadgl] Short but true story. I worked in Karumba in 1980 &1981 on a wharf unloading prawn trawlers.
They were the best prawns I have ever eaten. The sad thing was almost all of them were exported, even back then. There was so much money made from exporting them that it just made no sense to the owners to sell them in Aus.
Sadly it appears nothing has changed. Exporting the best stuff while importing a lesser product:(
[ihbh] Gees that's far away.
Did they fly it out?
Also, did each wharfie pocket a few as they unloaded the trawlers, or only the ones that fell on the wharf?
[revheadgl] Nah. I worked for A. Raptis & sons and almost all their boats had snap freezers. They were packed in 10kg plastic boxes and frozen on the boats. From there, into the factory, thawed, graded and refrozen and packed 20 or 26kg (I think?) cartons for shipping.
Later loaded into freezer shipping containers from a massive freezer room we had and then shipped to Brisbane and Adelaide And to the best of my memory overseas from there. They had a road train weekly for transport to Adelaide. Can't remember the frequency of trucks to Brisbane though. This was a long time ago. lol.
Also there were always at least 1 or 2 Japanese motherships that would buy directly and then take back to Japan. Only one I can remember the name of was Shinya Maru as we had a farewell for the crew. Was a fun night even though there was no shared language.
And, no we didn't steal them. No need, most skippers would give us a box or two after unloading. All they cared about was getting to the pub:)
And yes, I didn't eat a prawn for about 10 years after I left. Aversion by over consumption:)
[revheadgl] @SetTheFaqUp: Yep. I remember watching the process in the factory the for first time and thinking that's odd. They were only partially thawed, just enough to separate them for grading and sizing
And I vaguely recall they either used something in the initial pre freeze on the boats or during the later sorting and refreezing process. It was all pretty quick though. Might have been sodium metabisulfite? Like I said it was a long time ago, so I don't have total recall, lol.
[revheadgl] @SetTheFaqUp: Forgot to mention, there were maybe 3 or 4 small "wet boats" that we bought from sometimes. They were daily boats, and they cooked the prawns onboard in sea water and were delivered that way. They were the absolute best tasting, but I have no idea where they went from us after unloading them into the freezer room.
[Drakesy] Lets be honest, the deli sells the same prawns from vietnam.
[Jackson] All this pile on the Vietnamese, what happened to equal opportunity eaters?
[Lizard Spock] I mean no one's stopping you from enjoying overseas prawns. But we are an island nation girt by sea… Our land abounds in nature's gifts
of beauty rich and rare… Sorry, I got carried away there for a moment. We have the best and plentiful prawns right here, so it doesn't make much sense to buy a filter feeder from an oversea country with questionable water quality.
[Jackson] I am all for buying Australian and have spouted the virtues here myself a number of times, but we all have plenty of our own problems here according to many of OBers who have complained about our salmon farming practices, I don't expect our prawns are much different
[THEMAN_AUS] I bought a bag a couple of weeks back and it does taste a bit like ocean slavery
[cooni] What brands of Aussie prawns are there and how much are they when they go on sale?
All this Vietnam vs Australia talk needs to be backed up with prices.
[UNO] I've not seen these go on sale https://www.coles.com.au/product/karumba-raw-banana-prawn-me… .
[snappy1234] Wonder if that is due to Raptis prawning closing
( less competition)
[SetTheFaqUp] Wonder how can the VN prawns be so cheap…
Sure, you save on labour, and add the transport cost back in …
1. farmer profit
2. exporter handling charge
3. wholesaler/importer handling charge
4. supermarket mark up
[bargainhunter] https://www.coles.com.au/product/karumba-frozen-raw-banana-p…
Frequently $18kg, though it appears bulk only atm. Available in Qld and NSW at least.
[coolkidswag] Support capitalism and buy these prawns !
[tradewind] No thanks. Just grab some MSC certified wild caught prawns if you want prawns. These are garbage.
[takemymoney] Well any takeaway prawn dish is likely using this or similar…Karumba is great but this is cheap.
[Mild October] Got a dumb question.
Whats the difference between tail on and off?
[Nefe] I think it's the flavour. I do eat the tails, but I use the tails to cook any recipe with prawns. Without tails or heads, the prawn doesn't taste like a prawn.
[Blitzfx] The tail shell is still on, and you'll need to peel it off when you eat.
There are recipes which benefit with the tail shell on.
